title: The same finding from many reporters folds into one issue
iWant: ten reporters hitting the same defect on the same anchor to land as one issue with nine +1 comments carrying their environments, not ten separate issues
soThat: triage is cheap and duplicate storms do not swamp the tracker

acceptanceCriteria.description: fingerprint(entry) returns the first 12 hex chars of sha-256 over "<kind>|<targetKey>|<anchor>|<symptomClass>" where targetKey is the effective slug for blueprints (no version) or the verb path for core, anchor is upper-cased or "-" when absent, and symptomClass is one of the closed enum. Same fingerprint across two entries whose blueprint versions differ; different fingerprint when the anchor or class differs.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a fixture corpus of five entries: same-defect different-version, same-defect different-anchor, same-defect different-class, missing-anchor pair (title-only fallback), and one clean
acceptanceCriteria.when: fingerprint() is called on each entry
acceptanceCriteria.then: the versioned pair yields identical fingerprints; the anchor and class variants yield different fingerprints; the missing-anchor pair uses the "<kind>|<targetKey>|<symptomClass>|<normalisedTitle>" fallback (first eight tokens, punctuation and stop-words stripped, lower-case)

acceptanceCriteria.description: On submit, per pending entry, gh search issues is called for the destination repo with query "rcf-feedback-fingerprint: <fp>", --match body, --state open, --limit 5. Exactly one hit: gh issue comment on that number, comment body carries "+1 from another reporter" plus the Environment table and the redacted body only when it differs from the original by more than the environment lines. Zero hits: gh issue create. More than one hit: comment on the lowest number and mention the others.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a fake gh module (via RCF_FEEDBACK_GH_MODULE) whose search stub yields zero, one and two hits in three sequential invocations, and one pending entry per case
acceptanceCriteria.when: rcf feedback submit --yes runs three times
acceptanceCriteria.then: the zero-hit case calls gh issue create; the one-hit case calls gh issue comment on the returned number; the two-hit case calls gh issue comment on the smaller number and includes "also see #<other>" in the comment body

acceptanceCriteria.description: When gh search issues is unavailable or errors (rate-limit, GHES search off, non-zero exit), submit falls through to gh issue create for that entry and the state line stamps dedupe: unchecked. Closed issues are never matched; if --state closed search finds an issue with the same fingerprint the created new issue body carries "previously reported and closed as #<n>".
acceptanceCriteria.given: a fake gh module whose search stub throws for one call and returns a closed match for the next
acceptanceCriteria.when: rcf feedback submit --yes runs twice with one pending entry each
acceptanceCriteria.then: the first entry is created with dedupe: unchecked in state; the second is created with a body reference to the previously closed issue number
